title: Technical English — Course 5, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 6

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the review panel meet?
tasks.audioText: The engineering review panel will meet on Tuesday at eleven to consider a component replacement proposal. Students observing the meeting should bring the summary sheet and the inspection extract. The panel will compare the recorded condition, supplier information and expected service life. Any recommendation must identify the evidence used and note information that is still missing.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which two documents should observers bring?
tasks.audioText: The engineering review panel will meet on Tuesday at eleven to consider a component replacement proposal. Students observing the meeting should bring the summary sheet and the inspection extract. The panel will compare the recorded condition, supplier information and expected service life. Any recommendation must identify the evidence used and note information that is still missing.
options: The summary sheet and inspection extract

tasks.prompt: A replacement proposal compared two component options. Option A had a lower purchase cost, while Option B had a longer stated service life and a clearer maintenance record. The review team also considered delivery time and compatibility with the existing assembly. It did not select an option based on price alone; the recommendation explained how each factor affected the decision. Reading 1. Which advantage did Option B have?
options: A longer stated service life and clearer maintenance record

tasks.prompt: Why did the team avoid deciding on purchase price alone?
options: Because delivery time, compatibility and other factors also affected the decision

tasks.prompt: The recommendation ___ by the evidence in the review.
Choose TWO factors, other than purchase price, that may affect a replacement decision.
options: The colour of the supplier's logo

tasks.prompt: Information that supports a decision or conclusion is supporting ___.
A recommendation includes a claim without evidence. What should you ask?
options: The claim sounds convincing, so keep it.
Could we identify the record or source that supports this statement?
Evidence is not needed in a technical review.
I will remove the whole report.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of evidence-based decision in a logical order.
options: Compare cost, compatibility and service life
Define the decision to be made
State a recommendation with supporting evidence
correctOrder: Define the decision to be made
Compare cost, compatibility and service life
State a recommendation with supporting evidence

tasks.prompt: Write 100–120 words comparing two replacement options. Explain how cost, compatibility, service life and evidence should influence the recommendation.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: task completion and relevant content (0–2); clear organisation and logical linking (0–2); grammar and sentence structure (0–2); precise technical vocabulary, spelling and punctuation (0–2). Minor errors are acceptable if meaning remains clear.
